transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-06 15:00 UTC
Length: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE); Leah Kim (Redwood CSM); Samuel Reed (Northstar CTO); Priya Nair (Lead SRE); Caroline Wu (Platform Eng); Evan Torres (Security)

Summary:
Quick sync on the Private POC: latest stability/latency numbers, routing anomalies seen during the weekend, plan for a kernel-level patch in staging, and agreement on benchmarks/SLAs before ramping traffic. Agreed to run quantization + kernel trial and share updated canary runbook.

Topics covered:
- Weekend incident recap (egress surge + packet drops)
- Canary rollout rollback thresholds and circuit-breaker config
- Kernel/driver upgrade and quantization trial on staging
- Telemetry gaps (trace IDs dropping at the edge)
- Security / audit log retention and KMS questions

Action items (short): see action_items field above, we read them out at the end.

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya: okay good afternoon everyone, um thanks for joining our weekly POC sync. quick roll call?
00:07 Samuel: hi Sam Reed here, uh I'm the CTO at Northstar, thanks Maya.
00:10 Priya: Priya Nair, lead SRE, we were on-call over the weekend.
00:13 Caroline: Caroline, platform eng. we pulled some logs and have a couple examples.
00:17 Evan: Evan from security. short on time later but I'll stay for the key bits.
00:21 Maya: awesome, Leah too?
00:22 Leah: hi yeah Leah Kim CSM, quick note: we'll keep the agenda tight.
00:25 Daniel: Daniel Ortiz, SE — i'll drive the kernel/quant stuff.
00:29 Maya: great, first item: weekend incident. Priya, can you recap what you saw?
00:34 Priya: yeah so saturday around 03:15 UTC we saw a spike in egress for a subset of requests, roughly 12% packet retransmit increase, flows were coming from the east cluster. it coincided with a flurry of retries from the app tier, so latencies jumped p95 to 1.8s from baseline 450ms. logs show a number of TCP retransmits and also occasional PMTU blackhole signs, so might be an MTU mismatch on the overlay.
01:02 Daniel: ah, ok. so that could be the VXLAN MTU mismatch we've seen before in cloud provider CNI. did you also see any K-V cache miss storming? sometimes clients resend when the prefix cache isn't sticky.
01:12 Priya: we saw cache evictions but not at the magnitude the retries indicate. i wonder if the kernel offload path on our on-prem nodes dropped some segments. the NIC driver versions are a bit old.
01:22 Caroline: attaching a packet capture in the channel, but note the timestamps are a little off — recorder drift.
01:28 Maya: thanks. Daniel — what mitigations do you recommend short-term?
01:31 Daniel: immediate: pin MTU to 1400 on the overlay and enable jumbo-frame fallbacks on the host if possible, also increase our prefix KV cache TTL so transient miss storms don't amplify. medium-term: roll the kernel/driver patch Daniel mentioned which addresses an interrupt coalescing bug on certain NICs. we'll test that in staging first.
01:50 Samuel: what's the risk of the kernel roll? last time a driver tweak changed latency distribution a bit, we had to roll back.
01:56 Daniel: totally fair. risk is small but measurable — that's why we plan a canary with 5% traffic for 48 hours, with auto-rollback thresholds at 3x error-rate or 2x p95. we'll also keep a golden path in hosted zone so we can redirect.
02:12 Priya: can we get those thresholds codified? we need exact numbers for runbook.
02:16 Maya: yes, we'll share the canary thresholds doc after the call. i'll add it to the runbook link.
02:21 Leah: quick FYI, customer success will monitor during canary and call for a pause if SLOs breach.
02:26 Evan: security question — does the kernel change imply any differences in audit logs or syscalls we need to approve? we have an internal change review.
02:33 Daniel: the patch is driver-level, not user-space, so audit events shouldn't change, but we will provide a delta of the kernel modules and checksums. additionally we can sign the binaries and provide a signed artifact for your CM tools.
02:45 Samuel: sounds ok. one related thing: our compliance team wants a 7-year audit retention window for some logs — is that supported?
02:52 Maya: we support configurable retention in Private, but long-term retention may require integrating with your S3/GCS long-term store; we can include that as an enterprise add-on.
03:02 Caroline: on telemetry: we noticed some trace IDs drop off at the egress proxy, so root cause is unclear — instrumenting the proxy side might help.
03:09 Daniel: we recognized a gap where our front proxy didn't forward the trace header on certain error paths; we patched this last week, but we need to validate across the routing mesh.
03:18 Priya: ok can you run a synthetic that hits the proxy-heavy route and dump traces? we'll compare.
03:22 Daniel: yep i'll set up synthetic trace runs from staging and share the traces link.
03:26 Maya: next item: quantization kick-off and perf expectations. Daniel?
03:30 Daniel: we're proposing to run a 16-bit quant trial on a model slice to measure tail latency and token cost. expected perf: 10-18% token cost reduction, p95 might change by +/- 5% initially. we'll benchmark with the same prompt sets you used last week.
03:47 Priya: important for us is determinism under load — if quantization increases variance we'll need fallback to a 32-bit variant. do you have automatic fallbacks?
03:55 Daniel: yes, Redwood runtime supports model variant fallback with routing policy; we'll set a policy: if p95 delta > 20% or error-rate > 1% then fallback to base model.
04:08 Samuel: timeline to run quantization in staging and evaluate?
04:11 Daniel: I can kick off the trial after the kernel patch validation, so projected window is 2027-05-11 to 2027-05-13.
04:18 Caroline: please add the exact prompt set and replica sizing to the results doc — we must be able to reproduce.
04:23 Daniel: noted, will include config + seed prompts + seq lengths.
04:27 Maya: pricing question came up on your side — Priya, you mentioned dedicated reserved pool as a possibility?
04:32 Priya: yes for steady traffic we'd consider a reserved pool, but we still want burst capacity for unpredictable peaks. cost trade-offs are unclear.
04:39 Maya: we'll send a matrix: reserved commit tiers vs burst pricing vs on-demand. also include the latency guarantees per tier.
04:45 Samuel: and SLA for failover — what is the expected RTO for region fallback?
04:50 Daniel: region fallback is automated; typical RTO depends on DNS TTLs and route convergence but our measured median is ~60s for active fallback if circuit-breaker trips and route switches to hosted fallback. we'll put empirical numbers in the runbook.
05:03 Priya: any bandwidth shaping or egress limits we should configure to avoid weekend spikes?
05:08 Daniel: yes, we can apply token-bucket shaping at the routing layer per-customer and per-route. configuring a conservative burst window for the app tier helped the last time.
05:16 Caroline: one more item — can we get the exact kernel/driver version you'll use? ops wants that before any change window.
05:21 Daniel: sure: kernel-5.19.12-patch-rw1 and nic-driver 2.4.8 with checksum abc123 — i'll share the release artifact and signature.
05:31 Evan: security asks to scan the module binary; can you provide a reproducible build?
05:35 Daniel: yes we can provide reproducible builds and a signed artifact for your supply-chain review.
05:40 Maya: okay wrapping up. let's read action items back: Daniel will run kernel patch in staging and report by 2027-05-10; Priya will provide logs and heatmaps by 2027-05-09; Evan will confirm retention/KMS constraints; Maya will share pricing and canary runbook by 2027-05-07.
05:56 Samuel: all sounds good. can we plan a mid-canary check on day 1 of the canary?
06:00 Leah: yes CSM will schedule a 30-min mid-canary review and a post-canary retro.
06:05 Maya: perfect. i'll send calendar invites and the runbook link. thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
